subject: Clarify SLA: streaming TTFT vs sustained-throughput commitments
messages:
From: Samuel Turner <samuel.turner@banyanhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify TTFT vs sustained throughput in SLA for PoC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Redwood runtime looks promising for our chart summarization use case. Before we move forward with the POC procurement flow, legal and engineering at Banyan have a couple of very concrete asks about how you measure streaming vs non-streaming commitments:

- Our security/compliance team needs a clear definition of Time-To-First-Token (TTFT). Is TTFT measured from request ingest at the API gateway, from auth validation completion, or from the model runtime enqueue?
- For streaming endpoints, we need a documented expectation for sustained tokens/sec (we commonly see bursts during night-batch prep). Are throughput SLAs expressed as a sustained 1-minute window? 5-minute?
- If we need an exception (e.g., higher sustained bursts for a limited pilot), what does Redwood require to approve it? Is there a formal carveout process, and what data do you need?

We'd appreciate a short writeup and, if possible, a proposed carveout clause we can share with procurement. Happy to loop in Olivia (cc'd) who owns procurement.

Best,
Sam

Subject: Re: Clarify TTFT vs sustained throughput in SLA for PoC

Sam — great meeting yesterday, thanks for the concise list. I pulled together the short definitions and next steps below. Attaching a one-pager (SLA_metric_spec_v1.pdf) that we can use in the SOW.

Short answers (high level):
1) TTFT definition: We measure TTFT from the point the request is accepted by our edge API (after basic auth and quota checks). That maps to the server-side enqueue timestamp; any time spent in client-side retries or rtt is excluded. TTFT is reported as both P50/P90/P99 over the measurement interval.

2) Sustained throughput definition (streaming endpoints): We define sustained throughput as the 1-minute moving-window average of delivered tokens/sec to the client across successful stream connections, with percentile reporting (P50/P95/P99). Burst capacity and transient scheduler spikes are measured separately and do not count towards sustained throughput metrics if they are under a configurable burst-duration threshold (default 15s).

3) Carveout / exception process: For pilot carveouts (higher short-term sustained bursts or longer TTFT variance due to batch patterns), we need:
   - expected traffic profile (1-min and 5-min percentiles)
   - sample request IDs / anonymized traces for one representative day
   - target dates and max duration for the carveout (start/end)
   - proposed success criteria (e.g., 95% of requests meet P99 TTFT X ms)

If you provide that, we can run an internal capacity review and suggest either: a temporary reserved pool (Dedicated burst), a relaxed P99 for the pilot window, or an explicit SLA amendment for the initial contract term.

Next steps I propose:
- Banyan to share a 48-hour representative traffic dump + target pilot window (you mentioned a weekend batch).
- Redwood infra to validate and propose an exception path + any pricing delta.
- If approved, we issue a short amendment and include the SLA_metric_spec as an exhibit.

Subject: Re: Clarify TTFT vs sustained throughput in SLA for PoC

Kim — tagging a few implementation notes that will help the capacity review. Agree with the definitions; adding operational constraints we should include in the carveout proposal: 

- Measurement anchor: use Redwood server-side enqueue timestamp (t_enqueue) and first-output timestamp (t_first_token). TTFT = t_first_token - t_enqueue.
- Edge vs runtime skew: we may see up to ~40-80ms extra TTFT when requests are routed cross-region or if auth rules add hop -> call this out.
- Tokens/sec baseline: for model variants we will base sustained tokens/sec targets on a 1-minute moving window as Kimberly noted. However, for some quantized 4-bit kernels the per-GPU throughput differs; we should provide model-variant-specific throughput bands in the exhibit.
- Fallbacks: recommend an automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant when TTFT exceeds 2x expected median for >30s for more than 5% of connections in the pilot window.

I'll attach kernel notes and a short spreadsheet with model-variant throughput bands for the Banyan models you mentioned. If Banyan can provide a sanitized trace, infra will simulate load against our Dedicated pool and confirm bandwidth.

[Attachment: kernel-selection-notes.txt]
[Attachment: Banyan_MA_plan.xlsx]

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Clarify TTFT vs sustained throughput in SLA for PoC

Sam / Olivia — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Karthik's notes and our capacity review checklist, here is the proposed carveout approach we can include in the SOW:

Proposed pilot carveout (summary):
- Measurement: TTFT anchored at server enqueue; report P50/P95/P99 for the pilot window (daily). Sustained throughput = 1-minute moving-window average tokens/sec (P50/P95).
- Duration: pilot carveout window up to 30 days; extendable by mutual agreement.
- Thresholds: during the pilot we will accept up to a 20% relaxed P99 on TTFT for streaming endpoints vs signed SLA, provided sustained tokens/sec stays within the agreed bands.
- Fallbacks & mitigations: automatic model-variant fallback if TTFT exceeds 2x expected median for >30s affecting >5% of sessions; Redwood will notify Banyan and open a priority incident.
- Data required from Banyan: 48-hour sanitized traces, target pilot weekend, and a single point of contact for the runbook.
- Pricing: a small monthly premium for Dedicated burst capacity during the pilot — Redwood to provide a line-item.

If that looks reasonable, Olivia / Banyan procurement can approve and we'll route a short amendment and a DocuSign envelope for signatures. I've included a DocuSign link in the related_links field and attached the SLA spec & model notes for engineering review.

Best,
Kimberly
